extraction.Name: Charles O'Rourke
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not want the patent to his 160 acre allotment at the time he got it, but was advised that it was reported to the tax collector, and would finally be sold for taxes if he did not accept it, so he took it
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: gave Mr. Morris a deed to the land
extraction.Buyer: Mr. Corbon Morris, of Rapid City, South Dakota, who paid the taxes, and paid him about $300.00 in cash
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: by 1920, he had gotten behind in taxes, could not make the payment of them, so he procured a buyer
extraction.Occupation/Income: works for a cattle man, which is his chief source of income
extraction.NOTES: mentally competent; poor health, being bothered very much with his heart and throat; has a wife and five minor children to support, all the family having good health except one boy, who is a cripple for life, his spine being injured by a horse falling on him; finds it pretty hard to meet living expenses for his family out of his income; has never received any help from the County, State or United State Government; document dated November 21, 1928; allotment was 160 acres | ORIGINAL_TRIBE_VALUE: "Shannon County, South Dakota (Pine Ridge area implied)" (normalized 2026-04-28 to canonical 'Pine Ridge')
